business_scope.primary_industry_name: Income-Generating Real Estate Property Portfolio Trust (REIT)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: New Zealand (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (with statutory codification under the Companies Act 1993 and residual Crown/Te Tiriti o Waitangi principles)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Investment chapters of the New Zealand-China Free Trade Agreement (2008) and upgrade protocol
New Zealand-Australia Closer Economic Relations Investment Protocol
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Investment Chapter
New Zealand-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (entered into force 31 May 2023)
New Zealand-European Union Free Trade Agreement (entered into force 1 May 2024)
New Zealand-Hong Kong, China Closer Economic Partnership Agreement
Double Taxation Relief (Australia, United Kingdom, United States, China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, India, Canada, and 40+ other jurisdictions)
Agreement between New Zealand and the United States on Facilitating and Expediting Investment (Investment Facilitation Framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Act 2022; Companies Act 1993 (ss. 21-25, 206A-206M on beneficial ownership registers and refusal of names); Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulations 2023/2024; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Regulations 2014 (for licensed income-generating real estate portfolio trusts); Trusts Act 2019; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Privacy Act 2020.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — beneficial ownership information must be filed with the New Zealand Companies Office and is disclosed to competent authorities and supervised financial institutions under legal gateways; the register is not openly searchable by the public in the same manner as the company register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of foreign corporate constituent documents (certificate of incorporation and memorandum/articles of association), if a corporate shareholder or trustee is involved
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign registrar or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the originating state; where the originating state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention, full consular legalization by the New Zealand Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of no tax arrears from the ultimate parent or corporate founder's home registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign tax authority and/or company registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization chain (notarization, ministry of foreign affairs, and New Zealand consular attestation where required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all proposed directors, beneficial owners, and trust settlors/protectors/beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trusted notary public or issuing state passport office / national identity authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of notarized copy/signature block

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the New Zealand resident agent and any local licensed REIT manager or trustee
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the origin jurisdiction or New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (from origin state) or consular legalization if origin state is non-Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and ownership/control chain chart covering all natural persons exercising 25% or more ownership or effective control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Declarant beneficial owners before a notary public or authorized AML/CFT reporting entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarized declaration or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / AML/CFT customer due diligence confirmation from the source of funds bank, including FATCA/CRS entity classification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled bank statement/signature and capacity page; no consular legalization needed for bank-to-bank verification if recipient is a regulated NZ reporting entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List and Non-SDN Lists, US 561 List, UK HMT Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Australian DFAT Consolidated List, and New Zealand sanctions administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates of PEPs in accordance with AML/CFT Act 2009 ss. 12-19, including independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Sanctions screening must be repeated at every distribution event (dividend transfer) and prior to any change of directors, UBOs or Trustees.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online Company Register and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal — https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed name must be in Latin alphabetic characters; English and te reo Māori names are accepted. If a foreign-script legal name is desired, a Latin-script transliteration or translation must be filed and will appear on the register as the primary legal name. Names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, overseas company, NZBN entity, or reserved names are automatically refused. The Registrar applies a homophone and near-identical character test, including omission, addition, or substitution of the words 'Limited', 'LLP', 'Trust', 'Reit', 'Property', 'Capital', or 'Investment'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days of the Registrar's refusal, a written administrative appeal/reconsideration request must be lodged with the Registrar of Companies under Companies Act 1993 s. 25(3), attaching a proposed name comparison table and, where relevant, written approval from the relevant Minister or licensing authority for the sensitive token. The Registrar must issue a dated written decision. If the appeal is unsuccessful, judicial review before the New Zealand High Court is available as a secondary remedy. A fresh name reservation can be submitted immediately after rejection without penalty if the new name is substantively distinguishable from the refused name; a subsequent fee may apply only if manual examination is triggered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is acceptable solely for satisfying the Companies Act 1993 s. 201 requirement of a registered office in New Zealand, provided full address details and postal direction are maintained with the Companies Office. However, for an Income-Generating Real Estate Portfolio Trust (REIT) requiring a statutory licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the New Zealand-resident trustee/manager must maintain a physical operational office in New Zealand where records, books, UBO register, trust deed, and AML/CFT compliance files are accessible to regulators; a pure virtual office is not permissible as the sole compliance location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% annualised probability for a licensed REIT trustee/manager in New Zealand due to unannounced on-site inspections by the Financial Markets Authority, Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT supervisors, New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, and Companies Office compliance teams; the likelihood materially increases if adverse reports, suspicious transaction reports, or sanctions screening hits occur.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and statutory name clearance request (including homophone/confusingly similar screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory nil-reservation fee; no fee charged at name reservation stage under the Companies Office 2023 Fees Schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation filing with issue of Certificate of Incorporation and first NZBN / IRD registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (NZ$111.60 online incorporation fee, converted at prevailing exchange rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address service for one year (statutory address and service of process address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed New Zealand corporate service provider / registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a physical registered office in Auckland or Wellington

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent / company secretary and statutory record-keeping compliance for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand registered agent / corporate services firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under AML/CFT Act 2009 and Companies Act 1993 ongoing compliance duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register establishment, AML/CFT risk assessment, PEP and sanctions screening, and source-of-funds verification file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand-qualified AML/CFT compliance consultant or corporate attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended professional fee equivalent to approximately NZ$900 at prevailing hourly rates for AML/CFT and corporate due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization bundle for notarized passports, certificate of good standing, power of attorney, and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public plus competent authority (e.g. Foreign Ministry) and/or New Zealand consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government per-document tariff plus notary and courier fees; estimated for six-document authenticated bundle from a non-Hague or mixed-origin profile

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Payment-rails and bank account due diligence pack covering dividend distribution wire and ACH setup (bank reference, FATCA/CRS classification, transaction laundering controls)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Correspondent bank / receiving NZ financial institution / qualifying corporate treasury service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for account-opening UBO pack, sanctions screening, and electronic payment rail documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 12, 15-26, 42-44, 47-49, 128-134, 153 and 171-178; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, ss 5-10, 33-35 and 45-95; Overseas Investment Act 2005, ss 10-19 and Schedule 1; Building Act 2004, ss 40-44, 101-108 and 112-116; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, ss 36-49; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, ss 10-15 and 20-32.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online filing via the NZBN / Companies Register portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz); financial-market licensing through the Financial Markets Authority (FMA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application (New Zealand Companies Office online 'Incorporation Application') together with the company constitution, consents to act of all first directors, shareholder consents, registered office address, and application for a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Companies Act 1993. The International Company is formed as a no-par-value limited liability company with an initial subscribed capital of NZ$1.00 per ordinary share. No escrow account is statutorily required, but under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, subscription proceeds must be held in a segregated New Zealand bank trust/escrow account and may only be released after completed source-of-funds verification and customer due diligence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, ADOPTED AT A MEETING DULY CONVENED AND HELD AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], NEW ZEALAND, ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the company was incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 as an International Company limited by shares; AND WHEREAS the initial directorship and shareholding were approved in the incorporation application. NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The allotment of [NUMBER] fully paid ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each to the initial subscribers identified in the share register is approved, confirmed, and ratified; subscriptions are to be paid into the company's segregated trust account and released only upon completion of AML/CFT verification. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the company shall be [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand, such address to be recorded with the New Zealand Companies Office and maintained continuously for service of process; the directors authorise the engagement of [REGISTERED AGENT NAME] as the New Zealand registered agent and service provider. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [NAME] is appointed as Chairperson and Managing Director, [NAME] as Director, [NAME] as Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as AML/CFT Compliance Officer, each to hold office until removal by ordinary resolution or under the constitution. (4) GOVERNANCE: The company constitution, financial delegation policy, conflicts-of-interest policy, and internal controls are adopted and ratified. (5) LICENSING: The directors are directed to file all necessary applications with the Financial Markets Authority, the Overseas Investment Office, relevant territorial authorities, and all other regulatory bodies required for the real estate investment trust activities. RESOLVED by the unanimous consent of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / NZBN online name check portal, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Register to confirm the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing New Zealand registered company, overseas company, or registered trademark. Where necessary, file an electronic name approval/reservation request and pay any applicable fee. The proposed name should include the suffix 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English
Name search / availability record from the Companies Register
Registered trademark clearance certificate if the name contains a protected term
Director identification documents for the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a revised name, obtain and file the written consent of the owner of a similar name, or seek administrative review by the Registrar under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993; formal refusal may be appealed to the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Constitution and Governing Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial shareholders and first directors; independent legal counsel / notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft, approve, and execute the company constitution in English. The constitution must set out share classes, transfer restrictions, director powers, indemnity provisions, dividend policy, and dispute resolution mechanisms. Each first director must sign a consent to act as director and each first shareholder must subscribe to shares. If notarisation is required by a foreign shareholder or bank, the signatures must be notarially certified and apostilled.
required_dossiers: Company constitution duly executed by all subscribers
Consent to act as director for each first director
Written subscription agreement for each initial shareholder
Certified copy of each shareholder's passport and proof of residential address
Notarial certificate / apostille if required under overseas law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries defective constitutional provisions, the board may adopt a supplemental resolution or restate the affected clause and re-execute before incorporation; if the defect is jurisdictional, the company may submit corrected documents during the 10-working-day Companies Office query window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE; online via Companies Register (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online Company Incorporation Application to the Companies Office. Upload the signed constitution, consents to act, shareholding details, director details, registered office address, and agent consent. Pay the official filing fee. The Registrar will verify the application, issue the Certificate of Incorporation, and assign a unique company number and NZBN.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application
Company constitution in PDF
Consents to act of all directors
Shareholder subscription and consent form
Details of registered office and registered agent
AML/CFT identity verification package for directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant may correct the identified deficiencies through the online portal, file supplemental evidence, or apply for an extension of the statutory response period; an unlawful rejection may be appealed by way of judicial review to the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; registered agent approved to act in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the lease or service agreement for the registered office in New Zealand, and obtain the written consent of the registered agent. The registered office must be a physical address capable of receiving documents during business hours, not a postal-only box. The Companies Register must be updated with the address; the company must maintain statutory records at the registered office or at the registered agent's premises.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or service agreement
Letter of consent from the registered agent
Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation
Directors' identification and residential address confirmation
Statutory records maintenance acknowledgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or the address is rejected, the board must appoint a substitute agent and file a notice of change of registered office within 10 working days; failure to maintain a registered office may lead to removal by the Registrar, and the company may apply for restoration upon rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxation, Inland Revenue, and NZBN Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and New Zealand Customs / NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company's Inland Revenue Department number (IRD number), New Zealand Business Number, and any required GST registration if taxable supplies are anticipated or if voluntary GST registration is advantageous. For employees, register for PAYE; for a REIT investment trust, obtain confirmation of the applicable tax classification and any eligible exemption or portfolio investment allocation for non-resident shareholders.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and company number
Company constitution
Directors' and shareholders' tax identification numbers
Certified passport copies
NZBN/IRD online application form
Bank confirmation of the segregated trust account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD query or rejects the tax registration, the company may amend its online application, provide corrected proof of identity, or file an objection under the Tax Administration Act 1994; delayed filings may be cured by voluntary disclosure before enforcement action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FMA Managed Investment Scheme / REIT Licence Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the real estate investment trust, prepare the trust deed and supervisor agreement, prepare the product disclosure statement (PDS), and apply for registration of the managed investment scheme under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. The entity acting as manager must apply for a market services licence. The application must demonstrate that directors and senior managers are fit and proper with sound risk-management, conflict-management, AML/CFT, and investor-funds protection systems.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and constitution
REIT trust deed executed by manager and supervisor
Supervisor agreement with a licensed FMA supervisor
Product disclosure statement
Application for manager's market services licence (Form FMA)
AML/CFT compliance programme
Business plan and financial projections
Fit-and-proper statements for directors and senior managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA requests further information or proposes to decline, the applicant may submit written submissions, amend the documents, and offer binding undertakings. If licence conditions are imposed, the applicant may apply for an administrative variation of conditions; an adverse decision may be appealed under section 422 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Overseas Investment Office Consent for Land and Property Assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Overseas Investment Office (OIO), Land Information New Zealand (LINZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the REIT intends to acquire sensitive land, significant rural land, or significant business assets as defined in the Overseas Investment Act 2005, file an OIO consent application. The application must define the ownership chain, the property schedule, and the intended use, and must demonstrate that the investment will provide a material benefit to New Zealand. Obtain OIO consent before settlement or registration of any unconditional acquisition agreement.
required_dossiers: OIO online application form and fee receipt
Certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents
Ownership and corporate structure chart
Schedule of real estate assets to be acquired
Business plan and economic benefits assessment
Financial capacity statements, bank letters, and funding agreements
For sensitive land, a land-use and benefit analysis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OIO requests further information, the 20-working-day response clock may be extended by agreement; if consent is declined, the applicant may submit a new application incorporating additional public-benefit evidence, request reconsideration based on changed circumstances, or seek ministerial intervention under the Capital Investment Framework.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Building, Fire Safety, and Civil Defence Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial authority (city/district council); Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); licensed building inspectors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each real property held by the REIT, obtain or confirm a current building warrant of fitness, occupancy certificate, fire evacuation scheme approval, and civil defence/emergency plan. Arrange structural load inspections by a chartered professional engineer for any property that will house offices or significant equipment. Ensure compliance with the Building Act 2004 and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 before the properties are available for lease or occupancy.
required_dossiers: Building consent and completed as-built records
Maintenance schedule and current building warrant of fitness
FENZ fire safety compliance letter / evacuation scheme
Structural engineering load inspection report
Occupancy compliance certificate from the territorial authority
Civil defence and emergency response plan
Health and safety policy, worker information, and workplace risk register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a property fails inspection or the territorial authority issues a notice, the REIT may engage licensed contractors to remedy the defect, submit an application for re-inspection, and request a retrospective building certificate; hazardous-building determinations may be appealed under section 177 of the Building Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for the REIT managed investment scheme and manager licence; Overseas Investment Office (LINZ) for sensitive land consent; territorial authorities for building, land use, and resource consent; Fire and Emergency New Zealand for fire safety; WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational health and safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 – Registered Managed Investment Scheme (Real Estate Investment Trust) and Manager's Market Services Licence; Overseas Investment Office Consent (where applicable); Territorial Authority Building Owner's / Occupancy Compliance Certificate and Fire Safety Warrant of Fitness.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting with the relevant territorial authority and the Ministry for the Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration / Exempt for a passive income-producing real property trust with no new earthworks, subdivision, or discharge activities; Category 2 – Full EIA Report / Resource Consent Application under the Resource Management Act 1991 if the REIT undertakes new building development, land conversion, or activities exceeding Permitted Activity thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharges must connect to the public reticulated system or comply with resource consent limits; any stormwater or trade-waste discharge to receiving waters must meet the water-quality standards in the Resource Management Act 1991 s.107. VOC emissions: administrative head-office operations have negligible VOC emissions, but any HVAC refrigerants must comply with ozone-depleting substances and HFC phase-down rules under the Climate Change Response Act 2002. Waste handling: solid and hazardous wastes must be removed only through licensed waste operators and tracked in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; tenant leases must require compliance with environmental and hazardous-substances standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the REIT must hold and maintain FENZ-approved fire evacuation schemes, annual fire system inspection certificates, and building warrants of fitness under the Building Act 2004. Structural load: every occupied building must have a current structural engineering inspection verifying load capacity and seismic resistance in accordance with the building code. Occupational clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand health-and-safety notification, hazard identification, ventilation and exposure-monitoring, and emergency preparedness plans must be in place before operations; civil defence coordination with the territorial authority must be included in the approved emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; official online portal myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz); public website https://www.ird.govt.nz; complementary agency for customs/export procedures: New Zealand Customs Service (Trade Single Window).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the foreign entity carries on a taxable activity, has a New Zealand source of income, or is an overseas company 'carrying on business' in New Zealand within the meaning of the Companies Act 1993; if so, register with the New Zealand Companies Office as an overseas company, obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and appoint a New Zealand agent for service. Step 2: Apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number via myIR or the prescribed non-resident entity application form (including the IR 483 series), attaching certified constitutional documents, certificate of incorporation, director details, and evidence of the New Zealand agent/registered office. Step 3: Concurrently assess GST registration obligations: registration is compulsory if annual taxable supplies in New Zealand equal or exceed NZD 60,000, or if the non-resident entity supplies 'remote services' to New Zealand-resident consumers above that threshold; apply via myIR or form IR 356. Step 4: Voluntarily register for GST where a taxable activity exists even if below threshold, and maintain a New Zealand bank account to facilitate GST refunds and tax payments; for entities without a physical presence, appoint a New Zealand tax agent and maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing and source-income records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the Income Tax Act 2007, New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box system; the following statutory elections and classifications are available: (i) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB for closely held companies, allowing tax-transparent treatment; (ii) Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) election under subparts HL and HM, including listed PIEs that provide REIT-equivalent pooled real estate tax settings, with a 28% final tax at entity level and no further investor tax for qualifying investors; (iii) source-based territorial limitation, whereby non-resident companies are taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income and may otherwise be exempt; (iv) hybrid and branch mismatch rules under Part FH, superseding tax avoidance arrangements and requiring disclosure where mismatch outcomes arise; (v) GST branch registration election for an overseas company to register its New Zealand branch as a separate GST group member. The Tax Exempt Zone designation in the underlying metadata is respected only to the extent the entity has no New Zealand-sourced income and qualifies under an explicit exemption; it does not override the 28% corporate tax rate on New Zealand-sourced real estate income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value-added tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies per 12-month period (compulsory); non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (including digital, legal, financial, and certain advisory services supplied to New Zealand-resident consumers) are also required to register when New Zealand-resident consumer supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per 12-month period; voluntary registration is available to non-residents carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, subject to the remoteness and land-connection exceptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, prior authorisation, or digital stamping regime applies in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol interoperability network; from 1 July 2022, all public-sector agencies are obligated to receive Peppol-compliant e-invoices, so suppliers to government should maintain e-invoicing capability. GST-registered persons must issue or provide tax invoices (standard tax invoice, buyer-created tax invoice, or credit note) within 28 days of a supplier's request, and must retain sufficient contemporaneous records (including export shipping documents, bank remittance records, contracts, and board resolutions) to substantiate zero-rated and exported supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% GST applies when the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of supply, supplies goods for removal to the Chatham Islands or for use in certain approved overseas projects, and retains the statutory export evidence. Services: 0% GST applies to services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied to a non-resident while in New Zealand, are not 'connected with real property in New Zealand', and are not physically performed in New Zealand (subject to statutory exceptions for remote services under s 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985). For a New Zealand real estate investment trust, rental, leasing, and property management income connected to New Zealand land is standard-rated (or exempt for residential accommodation) and cannot be zero-rated; only genuinely offshore treasury, administrative, or technical advisory functions performed outside New Zealand for non-resident counterparties, and not connected with New Zealand real property, may qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (lodged via New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export within the statutory period
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence confirming receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a priority audit area for the Commissioner of Inland Revenue. Where the supporting documentation bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the zero-rating is reversed and output GST at 15% is assessed on the supply, together with use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent. Knowingly lodging false GST returns or falsifying export documents constitutes a criminal offence under s 143A, carrying imprisonment and/or fines. Overpaid GST refunds, including those generated through circular foreign-exchange flows or sham export arrangements, may be recovered under ss 75 and 113 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, and repeat offenders may be excluded from GST refund schemes and subjected to Commissioner-initiated audit and information-holding notices.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the apex monetary, prudential, and financial-stability authority; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises market conduct and AML/CFT compliance for financial institutions; and the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) separately administers the Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening applicable to non-resident acquisitions of sensitive New Zealand land. All foreign-exchange dealing and liquidity clearing are performed by registered banks under the Reserve Bank's prudential supervision framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is an independently floating currency with fully open capital and current account convertibility. New Zealand has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations on current international payments, and all statutory exchange controls were abolished following the repeal of the Exchange Control Act 1953 in the mid-1980s. There are no conversion quotas, no exchange-control licensing requirements, and no prior central-bank approval for cross-border capital injections, dividend distributions, or repatriation of property-sale proceeds. For a Real Estate Investment Trust structured as a tax-exempt-zone International Company, the only material monetization frictions are tax-related (non-resident withholding tax on distributions and foreign investment fund classification for non-resident owners) and regulatory (Overseas Investment Act consent for non-resident acquisition of New Zealand land), neither of which restricts currency convertibility or wire clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable under New Zealand law: the jurisdiction maintains no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio into NZD. Export and any other foreign-currency receipts may be retained, converted, or disbursed at the account holder's absolute discretion. For the REIT, core operating income comprises NZD-denominated domestic rental receipts collected via local clearing rails; where incidental foreign-currency proceeds arise (e.g., disposal of an offshore property holding), they may be held in a multi-currency account at the Tier-1 bank or converted through the bank's FX desk without any notification to the Reserve Bank. The sole compliance duty is documentary: the REIT must maintain a source-of-funds and foreign-currency treasury ledger to satisfy AML/CFT monitoring expectations for credits at or above NZD 10,000 equivalent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (master treasury and FX settlement) / Capital Escrow Account (unit-holder contributions pending property settlement)
Operational Account (rental income concentration and expense clearing) / Trust Cash Account (segregated distributable cash reserves)
Operational Account (dividend disbursement and tax clearing) / Escrow Account (acquisition deposits)
Multi-Currency Account (NZD, AUD, USD) for cross-border distributions / Operational Account (tenant receipting)
Operational Account (domestic Direct Debit and ACH origination for recurring distributions) / Term Deposit Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary rail; Low as a primary settlement venue. Offshore digital EMI platforms (UK FCA-registered payment institutions or EU PSD2 e-money institutions) are operationally feasible for low-value, recurring dividend wires to international unitholders and for minor foreign-currency conversions, but they cannot substitute for a Tier-1 New Zealand commercial bank. Legal and practical constraints: (i) EMIs lack access to the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), so they cannot effect real-time NZD clearing; (ii) they are not registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act and their custodial sub-structure introduces unregulated counterparty risk in a REIT context; (iii) mortgage and mezzanine lenders will not recognize EMI balance screens for drawdown conditions; and (iv) the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 supervisor requirements and the trust deed restrict where rental income may be held. The treasury blueprint mandates that all rental concentration, capital escrow, and reserve accounts remain at a Tier-1 NZ bank, with EMI accounts used only as a displacement mechanism for outbound distributions under an executed counterparty-risk opinion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule requires directors to appear physically at a New Zealand bank branch for corporate account opening. The Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 permits non-face-to-face customer verification using acceptable verification methods, including digital identity verification (RealMe or providers operating under the New Zealand Digital Identity Trust Framework) and remote video interviews; all five Tier-1 banks routinely onboard low-risk New Zealand corporates without branch attendance. Nevertheless, practical underwriting of a tax-exempt-zone International Company (CK_IC) controlled directly or indirectly by non-resident shareholders will normally require escalation: a certified (notarized) corporate AML pack, a video compliance interview with the compliance officer, and, for several institutions, one in-person meeting in Auckland or Wellington with the designated director, the REIT manager, or the locally appointed principal officer. The blueprint recommends (i) appointing a New Zealand-resident director or manager to attend the physical interview, (ii) pre-certifying the entire corporate registry pack through a notary public, and (iii) evidencing a physical New Zealand operating address via lease or title, as a bare registered-office mailbox slot is a recognized onboarding blocker for this entity class.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt-zone International Company (CK_IC) controlled by non-resident shareholders seeking to acquire New Zealand income-generating real estate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Overseas Investment Office (OIO) consent decision or exemption certificate under the Overseas Investment Act 2005; complete chain-of-ownership and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) certification; audited financial statements and a source-of-wealth memorandum; the executed REIT trust deed and unit register; and a five-year commercial operating plan demonstrating arm's-length rental activity rather than passive tax-motive ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or bare-trustee shareholding with a registered-office mailbox as the only New Zealand address, triggering the 'shell company' red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of good standing issued within 90 days of application; certified register of directors and shareholders; evidence of physical New Zealand presence (lease agreement or freehold title); an IRD tax-file-number letter or non-resident tax status certificate; and a board resolution expressly authorizing the banking relationship and identifying the REIT's treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity rental income flows or concentrated dividend wires to foreign unitholders without visible tax disclosure, raising NRWT evasion concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IRD registration certificate and New Zealand tax file number; unit-holder register and distribution policy; filed non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) returns with dividend reconciliation schedules; and audited cash-flow statements matching property-level rents to declared unit-holder distributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an affiliated offshore entity exceeding NZD 50,000 equivalent without a recognizable SWIFT purpose code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; board minutes approving the injection; a pre-notification funds-destination letter to the receiving bank; the remitter's source-of-funds confirmation from its licensed bank; and the consolidated group financial statements evidencing treasury capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media identifier attached to a UBO or a significant tenant counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent global sanctions and PEP screening report; legal opinion on the beneficial-ownership chain; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire and negative-media search log; and documentary proof of commercial nexus for any state-owned or politically exposed counterparty, together with a remediation undertaking acceptable to the bank's compliance committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 credits in NZD, USD, or AUD to the REIT's designated Tier-1 operational or capital-escrow account. The remitter must complete the SWIFT purpose-code field with 'EQUI' for equity subscription proceeds, 'CPIC' for cash capital contributions, or 'LOAN' for intercompany shareholder advances, and must reference the entity legal name plus the IRD and GST numbers in the narrative. Where the injection funds a New Zealand land acquisition, the OIO consent or exemption certificate (if the acquirer is an overseas person under the Overseas Investment Act 2005) must be in force and lodged with the receiving bank before settlement to avoid a transaction-monitoring escalation. Verification protocol: (i) any single credit at or above NZD 10,000 equivalent is subject to source-of-funds review; (ii) same-day aggregate credits above NZD 50,000 equivalent are conditionally cleared against a pre-approved funding matrix signed by the REIT manager; (iii) the bank will not require any Reserve Bank conversion license or surrender approval because NZD is fully convertible; and (iv) the complete MT103 chain, purpose codes, and funds-destination letters must be archived for at least five years to satisfy AML/CFT record-keeping obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary cross-border disbursement rail is SWIFT MT103 for dividend distributions, escrow releases, and overseas trade payments, using purpose codes 'DIV' for distributions, 'OTHR' for general trade settlement, or 'GOOD' for merchandise-related payments, as applicable. Domestic NZD clearing, including property completion settlements and tenant rebates, is executed through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), New Zealand's real-time gross settlement infrastructure, or through Direct Debit / ACH origination for recurring pre-authorized trust distributions. Where the REIT acquires property from a vendor's solicitor, the compliant bridge is an ESAS RTGS transfer from the REIT escrow account to the solicitor's trust account; a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) is an acceptable alternative where the counterparty requires trade-finance security. Dividend disbursement protocol for international unitholders: compute the NRWT withholding at the applicable statutory rate or the reduced rate prescribed by the relevant double-tax agreement; execute a single professional FX conversion on the aggregate distribution amount rather than per-beneficiary conversions; batch the payments into one MT103 file with a detailed beneficiary schedule; and archive the payment file and bank confirmation for the IRD dividend reconciliation and year-end audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts on the NZD/USD or NZD/AUD pairs with maximum tenor of twelve months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a registered New Zealand bank counterparty, limited to hedging forecast rental income conversions, dividend distributions, or property-sale receivables.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts referencing the NZD, documented under an NDF Annex or the ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions, permitted only where a deliverable forward market is inaccessible to a counterparty and the NDF is tied to an underlying real exposure of the REIT; speculative or thinly documented NDFs are prohibited by the treasury policy.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between NZD and USD or AUD to convert the REIT's floating-rate mortgage liabilities into fixed-rate foreign-currency obligations, executed under ISDA 2002 with a Credit Support Annex and subject to daily mark-to-market collateralization.

European-style FX vanilla options on NZD pairs used to hedge the acquisition price of an offshore asset or the repatriation of sale proceeds, with premiums expensed in the period and a strict no-speculative-overlay rule.

New Zealand dollar interest rate swaps referencing the Official Cash Rate (OCR) overnight index and 90-day bank-bill rates for managing the REIT's floating debt portfolio, subject to the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 derivatives licensing exemptions and the trustee's investment-statement authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Office filing) pursuant to sections 208-214 of the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary date of incorporation; the return period is the 12-month cycle ending on the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines for the company and each director (up to NZD 10,000); continued non-compliance permits the Registrar to issue formal notice and apply to strike the company off the New Zealand Register, followed by dissolution under sections 317-321 of the Companies Act 1993

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (audited where applicable) lodged with the Registrar and, for FMC reporting entities, the Financial Markets Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies / Financial Markets Authority (FMA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: FMC reporting entities: within 4 months after balance date; large non-FMC entities: within 6 months after balance date; small and medium non-FMC entities are exempt unless audited financial statements are required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors face fines up to NZD 10,000 under the Companies Act 1993; FMC reporting entities face civil liability and FMA enforcement orders for late or inaccurate financial reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return (company income tax return or nil-return filing with Inland Revenue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date: due 7 July; for a non-standard balance date: due the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date; tax agent time-of-use extensions may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month-end occurrence, incremental late filing charges, automatic default assessments, and use-of-money interest on unpaid tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Program Review and Customer Due Diligence (UBO) Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as AML/CFT supervisor; confirmation filed internally with the registered agent and available for FMA inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 12 months of the prior review date; no fixed statutory calendar date applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory orders, compliance remediation plans, and civil penalties up to NZD 2,000,000 for entities and NZD 50,000 for officers under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Annual Confirmation (address and agent validation via the New Zealand Business Number record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Coincident with the Annual Return deadline on the incorporation anniversary; any change of registered office or agent must be notified within 20 working days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a valid registered office and registered agent in New Zealand renders the company non-compliant under sections 188-190 of the Companies Act 1993 and is a ground for removal from the Register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit applies where the entity is an FMC reporting entity, is a managed investment scheme or licensed REIT under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, qualifies as a 'large company' (revenue NZD 30 million or more, or total assets NZD 60 million or more), or where shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting shares request an audit under section 199 of the Companies Act 1993
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for FMC reporting entities and large companies; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for other reporting entities; local New Zealand GAAP for non-reporting entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently maintain a public beneficial ownership register; instead, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 requires the REIT entity to verify and record the beneficial ownership of all unit holders and shareholders at establishment, on any material transfer, and through an annual AML/CFT compliance program review. The Companies Act 1993 additionally requires that every transfer of shares be recorded in the share register and that director appointments or resignations be filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Financial Records and Statutory Accounting Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a REIT of average complexity; USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 where a full statutory audit is not mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in New Zealand. The headline corporate rate of 28% applies to all resident companies and to non-resident companies deriving New Zealand-sourced income. Preferential taxation arises through the dividend imputation system, under which New Zealand-resident shareholders receiving fully imputed dividends are taxed on the grossed-up amount at their marginal rate and receive a credit for the 28% corporate tax paid. For listed property vehicles and qualifying collective investment structures, the Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) rules provide conduit taxation with a maximum prescribed investor rate of 28% and generally no tax on capital gains from qualifying REIT unit sales. New Zealand does not impose comprehensive capital gains tax; gains on real estate are taxable only if derived from a profit-making scheme, dealing, or development activity. Certain R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation on commercial fit-out may reduce the effective corporate rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - company income tax return, filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR Secure Online Services portal; approved software providers may transmit IR4 returns via the Inland Revenue Gateway. Related provisional tax and terminal tax schedules are processed through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (IR4 return); provisional tax instalments are filed three times per year for a standard balance date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard balance date of 31 March, provisional tax instalments are due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May; terminal tax is due 7 April following the balance date; the annual IR4 return must be filed no later than 7 July following the balance date. Non-standard balance dates have aligned filing dates with the first day of the fourth month after balance date in the case of the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all assessable income derived from the New Zealand-source real estate portfolio, including rental income, property management fees, taxable distributions from the REIT, and assessable gains from properties held on revenue account. Attach a reconciliation of each property's rental schedule and capital expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company not managed and controlled in New Zealand reports only New Zealand-source income in the IR4. Foreign-source income is excluded from the New Zealand tax base unless the company is, in substance and fact, managed in New Zealand and therefore New Zealand tax resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1B - Exempt income and non-assessable items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify exempt dividends, capital returns, non-taxable capital gains, and amounts that are not assessable under the Income Tax Act 2007. These amounts must be separately reconciled to prevent double inclusion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A capital gain realised outside a dealing or profit-making scheme is generally non-assessable for the non-resident. Distributions of REIT capital returns should be excluded from gross income but must be documented with the REIT's distribution statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim expenses wholly or partly incurred in deriving assessable income: property rates, insurance, maintenance and repair, property management fees, borrowing costs, statutory depreciation, legal and accounting fees, and apportioned head-office overheads. Non-deductible items include private expenditure, capital losses, statutory fines, and entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, deductible expenses must be apportioned on a reasonable basis to the New Zealand source. Interest deductions may be restricted by the thin capitalisation rules if the IC's New Zealand debt-to-asset ratio exceeds the allowable benchmark, and cross-border service fees must satisfy arm's length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Net taxable income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after statutory deductions and adjustments. If a tax loss results, carry it forward under the shareholder continuity and business continuity rules for set-off against future taxable income in accordance with the applicable carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be specifically connected to the New Zealand business or property portfolio. A non-resident may carry forward a New Zealand branch loss only if the same business is continued with substantially the same ownership and the loss has an economic nexus to the New Zealand source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Imputation credits and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record imputation credits attached to dividends received from New Zealand-resident companies, resident withholding tax credits, non-resident withholding tax credits, and foreign tax credits claimed under a DTA. Supporting dividend statements and tax credit certificates must be retained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits are not refundable to non-resident shareholders. Dividends paid to the non-resident IC are normally subject to non-resident withholding tax at source; treaty relief requires the beneficial owner to hold a valid tax residence certificate and submit it to the paying entity before the distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax payable / terminal tax / refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile provisional tax already paid, the RWT/NRWT credits, imputation credits, and terminal tax due. Calculate the final corporate tax liability or refund and provide payment instructions for any terminal tax balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident IC must ensure that NRWT was correctly deducted on all distributions. If a DTA reduced rate was not applied at source because the TRC was not available, the IC may file a refund claim with Inland Revenue within the statutory period, attaching the TRC, dividend statements, and an explanation of beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 incurs a late filing penalty of NZD 50 for each month or part-month the return remains unfiled, subject to a maximum of NZD 500. Unpaid terminal tax and provisional tax face late payment penalties of 1% per month on the amount outstanding, plus use-of-money interest. Deliberate failure or gross carelessness may trigger shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall and criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) rate on dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company to a non-resident shareholder is 30%. Under New Zealand's double tax agreements, the treaty rate is commonly reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% to 25% of the voting power, depending on the applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) establish that the relevant double tax agreement with its residence jurisdiction is in force and includes a dividend article; (2) obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (3) complete the Inland Revenue non-resident withholding tax declaration or the foreign certificate of residence form recognised by New Zealand; (4) deliver the TRC and a statement of beneficial ownership to the New Zealand-paying entity before the distribution date; and (5) ensure the payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source. If treaty relief is not applied at source, the non-resident may file an IRD refund claim for the excess NRWT within the statutory time bar, attaching the TRC and full distribution documentation. The payer must keep all treaty relief documentation in its contemporaneous records for audit verification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT rates for cross-border interest and royalties are 15%. New Zealand also permits an approved issuer levy (AIL) of 2% to be substituted for NRWT on interest paid to non-residents by an approved New Zealand issuer, provided the lender is not associated with the borrower and the loan has certain characteristics. Treaty-protocol rates for interest commonly range from 15% to 10%, and may be nil for interest paid to government financial institutions; royalty treaty rates are generally reduced from 15% to 10% or 5% depending on the type of intellectual property and the treaty partner. Royalties and interest must be paid gross only if the relevant NRWT obligation has been satisfied or a valid exemption and treaty certificate are on file.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand transfer pricing documentation thresholds are NZD-denominated: a Master File and Local File must be prepared and retained when the New Zealand taxpayer's cross-border related-party transactions in a category exceed NZD 10,000,000 per income year and the multinational group's global consolidated turnover exceeds NZD 100,000,000. Country-by-Country Reporting is separately required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue of at least NZD 1,000,000,000. Below those thresholds, taxpayers must still maintain sufficient records substantiating arm's length pricing under the Tax Administration Act 1994.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain named Economic Substance Regulations of the type found in zero-tax offshore centres. Instead, the Income Tax Act 2007, incl. the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1, applies a substance-over-form doctrine. An International Company established in an offshore tax-exempt zone must demonstrate genuine economic substance in its residence jurisdiction and cannot rely on a mere mailbox, nominee directors, or a single corporate service provider. If central management and control, board decision-making, real estate management, financing, or asset supervision is exercised in New Zealand, the entity is treated as a New Zealand tax resident and is taxed on worldwide income. Furthermore, the presence of a fixed place of business, or a dependent agent in New Zealand acting for the IC, constitutes a permanent establishment and requires New Zealand corporate tax compliance on the REIT income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating New Zealand-source REIT income, fabricating rental schedules, creating false invoices for management services, backdating board minutes, or using a zero-tax International Company to conceal the true beneficial ownership of distributable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A tax shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax, late payment penalties of 1% per month, and use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 may result in conviction, substantial fines, and imprisonment for up to five years; court-ordered reparation and confiscation of proceeds may also be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, approve, or participate in evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. The corporate veil is pierced by fraudulent conduct, allowing Inland Revenue to pursue personal assets. Directors may be subject to travel bans, asset freezing orders, and criminal imprisonment; disqualification as directors under the Companies Act 1993 may follow a conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / No Economic Substance / GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a shell: no employees, no physical office, no bank account in the nominal residence jurisdiction, no board meetings or minutes, and all REIT decisions are made in New Zealand by resident directors or shadow shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may disregard the shell entity and reconstruct the arrangements under section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. The income is reallocated to the person or entity with real control and economic ownership, assessed at 28% plus shortfall penalties (100% for an abusive tax position or 150% for evasion), and interest. The IC may also be denied DTA benefits under the principal-purpose test of the relevant treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and promoters of the shell arrangement face personal assessments as tax representatives, civil penalties, disqualification, and personal liability for company debts where the company was used for fraudulent trading; travel restrictions may be imposed and personal assets may be reached through civil recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CTF) Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving or distributing REIT dividends, management fees, or sale proceeds without performing customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, source-of-funds checks, or obligations reporting; using nominee shareholders or bearer structures to disguise the principal owner; wiring funds to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions without corresponding compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory action under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: civil penalty orders, infringement notices, compliance remedies, and suspension or cancellation of the reporting entity's registration. Money laundering offences under the Crimes Act 1961 can result in imprisonment of up to seven years; criminal proceeds are subject to forfeiture under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, senior managers, and compliance officers may be held personally liable for failing to establish or maintain an adequate AML/CTF programme. Knowing involvement in money laundering triggers personal criminal liability, imprisonment, travel bans, and confiscation of personal property; the corporate veil does not shield a director who controls the transaction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax and Profit Repatriation Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or technical fees from the New Zealand REIT to the International Company without deducting NRWT, mischaracterising dividends as tax-exempt loan repayments or return-of-capital, or claiming treaty relief without a valid tax residence certificate and beneficial ownership documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is personally liable for the NRWT that should have been withheld. A failure to withhold cannot be cured by later voluntary payment by the recipient. Late payment penalties, monthly incremental penalties, interest, and shortfall penalties of up to 100% apply. Criminal charges may be brought for deliberate avoidance of withholding tax obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise or accept non-withholding are personally liable for the unwithheld tax under the withholding tax regime. Civil recovery may enforce against the director's personal bank accounts and assets; travel bans and prosecution may follow; the corporate entity's separate legal personality will be disregarded where there has been fraud or sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, lease rentals, guarantee fees, or interest between the tax-exempt International Company and the New Zealand REIT so as to drain taxable profits offshore, or failing to prepare a Master File and Local File when related-party transaction thresholds of NZD 10,000,000 per category and group revenue of NZD 100,000,000 are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue will adjust the transfer price to an arm's length standard under the Income Tax Act 2007, increasing taxable income and issuing amended assessments. Shortfall penalties may range from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 40% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion-related conduct. Use-of-money interest accrues from the date the additional tax should have been paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing documentation knowing it to be false, or who direct pricing policies with the dominant purpose of tax avoidance, may be personally liable for penalties and interest. Inland Revenue can seek director penalty notices and pursue restitution where withholding tax, GST, or PAYE obligations are used as part of the profit-shifting arrangement. Directors who are merely wilfully blind are not protected by the corporate veil and may be prosecuted for aiding and abetting tax evasion.
